scores.evidence: Phase 0 op format `{ op: "insert", pos: 0, text: "Hello", id: "user1", clock: 1 }` while also claiming Yjs CRDT; "Yjs performs automatic CRDR merge"
scores.rationale: Positional ops contradict CRDT, Yjs described as 'server state machine', 'single-writer' claimed necessary for CRDT, Redis Pub/Sub plus 'optimistic locking' are muddled, and the DB schema stores position/text ops rather than Yjs updates.

scores.evidence: A multi-user real-time document editor where changes propagate instantly across all clients, including concurrent edits, presence indicators, and version history.
scores.rationale: It targets real collaboration with CRDT, persistence, offline and scaling, but the document is plain text with no rich-text model, and auth and permissions are deferred, so core needs are missing.

scores.evidence: Phase 0 "in-memory operation log (no database yet)" yet the persistence decision says the Phase 1 "WAL file"; Phase 3 exit check runs V3 while V3 is listed as phase 2
scores.rationale: The design is recognizable, but there are inconsistencies: positional ops vs Yjs, Redis Pub/Sub vs a single writer, V-labels and phases mismatched, and DB-down 'writes queue locally' conflicts with ACK-after-durable.

scores.evidence: Load test: 50 concurrent clients, 10 edits/sec per client, 10 sec duration, all edits at same position (high contention)
scores.rationale: It has concrete tests, crash recovery and chaos tests with early spike validation, but no randomized or property-based convergence testing, several invented thresholds, and the load test is a latency test rather than a convergence test.

scores.evidence: UNKNOWN: depends on product scale; supplied by product owner before Phase 4
scores.rationale: Assumptions and unknowns are labeled and many numbers are marked ASSUMPTION, though some thresholds like '<1 GB per 10 users' and the 'REQUIREMENT' label on 500 ms are unsupported.

scores.evidence: Chaos test: "Randomly kill backend instances, fail database, lose messages in broker. Verify: client reconnects within 10 s, no edit is lost"
scores.rationale: It covers crash, DB failure, CAS compaction races, offline duplicates and rate limiting, but misses malicious edit input, authorization failures, and corruption from clients, and the chaos test is late.

scores.evidence: Grafana with Prometheus scrape (backend exports `edits_received`, `clients_connected`, `broadcast_latency_ms`); alert if `clients_connected == 0`
scores.rationale: Metrics, SLO/alerts, feature flags and rollback are covered, but incident ownership, protocol-version rollout and a rolling-deploy story are absent, and some rollbacks are hand-wavy.

scores.evidence: Storage cost | N/A — persisted edits grow with doc history | UNKNOWN: retention policy
scores.rationale: Cost is barely treated: storage is left unknown, with no compute, broker or people costs and no cost controls beyond quotas.

scores.evidence: Conflict-free algorithm: OT vs CRDT | R3 (months rework; integration, undo, compaction differ...) | Default CRDT (Yjs or Automerge)
scores.rationale: A reversibility rating per decision with early spikes and revisit triggers is strong, though it misses lock-in on persisted op format and schema, and rates some choices oddly.

scores.evidence: Multi-doc sharding with "service discovery (etcd, Consul, or Kubernetes DNS)"; "helm chart stub"; OT spike implemented alongside Yjs
scores.rationale: Mostly phased, but it builds a parallel OT implementation, sharding and a conflict-visualization UX, while omitting essentials like auth and a rich-text model.

scores.evidence: Exit check: V1 passes (CRDT latency < 200 ms, undo reliable). V2 checkpoint test passes: 10k ops written, snapshot + tail consistent
scores.rationale: It has a concrete phase order with evidence and exit checks and a thin-slice first, though the model inconsistencies and mislabeled validations would need rework.

checklist.evidence: Default (chosen now) | CRDT (Yjs or Automerge) ... OT easier to understand but undo/redo and offline-first are simpler with CRDT
Operations are durably written to the database before ACK to client (satisfies RPO < 1 op)
use consistent hashing (or Redis cluster) to shard rooms by document ID
local edits are applied to local CRDT copy and stored in IndexedDB. When back online, Yjs performs automatic CRDR merge
Currently, all users on a document can read and edit.
Client-side undo affects only local CRDT; redo restores it.
Separate ephemeral channel (WebSocket message, not logged)
Phase 1 — Merge algorithm validation & persistence design
Measure join latency for doc with 100k ops; target < 2 s

traps.evidence: Phase 1 — Merge algorithm validation & persistence design
Operations are durably written to the database before ACK to client
When back online, Yjs performs automatic CRDR merge ... CRDT merge is conflict-free (no choice needed)

note: The plan has a sound build order (sync, persistence and spikes first) and a good decision-reversibility table, but it's technically muddled on CRDT vs positional ops. It also has no rich-text model, no authorization, no convergence fuzzing and weak cost analysis.
